title: PR #47050 added the project-scoped rule snooze (mute) endpoint, which loads the issue/metric alert rule by id alone without scoping it to the project in the URL, so a user can mute alert rules in other organizations.

findings.explanation: The code uses Django ORM with parameterized queries (Rule.objects.get(id=rule_id) and AlertRule.objects.get(id=rule_id)). The rule_id is extracted from the URL pattern as a named group and passed as a parameter to the ORM, which automatically handles parameterization. No string concatenation or raw SQL is used.

The endpoint fetches a Rule or AlertRule by user-controlled rule_id without verifying that the rule belongs to the project. The ProjectAlertRulePermission class is used, but the actual rule ownership check is missing. The can_edit_alert_rule function checks team/organization membership for the user but does not verify that the rule being accessed belongs to the project being accessed. An attacker could potentially snooze a rule from a different project if they have any access to the current project.
findings.suggested_fix: After fetching the rule, verify it belongs to the project: add a check like `if issue_alert_rule and issue_alert_rule.project_id != project.id: raise ValidationError(...)` similarly for AlertRule to ensure the accessed rule is from the correct project.
